blocks.title: Bestellen bleibt höflich
blocks.bodyEnglish: Ordering is one of the few situations where Germans stay formal — 'Sie' with a shopkeeper is normal even in a small village café. The one relaxed exception: dropping the verb entirely and saying just 'Einen Kaffee, bitte'.

blocks.headline: Einen, bitte — der Akkusativ
blocks.bodyGerman:
der Kaffee  →  einen Kaffee     (masculine shifts)
die Milch   →  eine Milch      (feminine stays)
das Wasser  →  ein Wasser      (neuter stays)
blocks.bodyEnglish: When a masculine noun is the thing you WANT (the direct object), 'der' becomes 'den' and 'ein' becomes 'einen'. Feminine and neuter don't change. This is the accusative case — you already use it every time you order something.

blocks.title: Bestellen
blocks.explanationEnglish: 'Ich möchte' (I would like) is the polite workhorse of every order. 'Ich hätte gern' is a notch more formal and sounds perfectly natural — either is safe.

examples.german: Ich hätte gern einen Tee mit Zitrone.
examples.english: I'd prefer a tea with lemon.

blocks.explanationEnglish: The accusative case marks the thing you act ON. Only masculine nouns change: 'der' → 'den', 'ein' → 'einen', 'kein' → 'keinen'. Feminine, neuter and plural look identical to the nominative. Order anything masculine and you've used the accusative.
blocks.englishBridge: English lost its cases, so there's nothing to compare — just memorise the masculine flip. 'A coffee' as a customer is ALWAYS 'einen Kaffee'.
blocks.targetSentenceEnglish: I would like a coffee, please.

blocks.title: »ein Kaffee« beim Bestellen
blocks.bodyEnglish: Masculine is the only gender that shifts. Ordering: 'ein Kaffee' ✗ → 'einen Kaffee' ✓. Feminine and neuter stay as they are: 'eine Milch', 'ein Wasser'.

blocks.prompt: Ordne jedem deutschen Wort die richtige Übersetzung zu.

blocks.explanationEnglish: 'der Kaffee' is masculine, and as the thing you want it shifts to the accusative: 'einen Kaffee'.
'Stück' is neuter, so the article stays 'ein': 'Ein Stück Kuchen'. Serving sizes come before the noun.

blocks.prompt: Which stays unchanged in the accusative?
blocks.explanationEnglish: Only masculine shifts. 'die Milch' is feminine, so it stays 'eine Milch'.

blocks.promptEnglish: Build: 'Ich möchte einen Tee mit Zitrone.'

blocks.title: Bestellen in einer Zeile
bullets: Ich möchte … / Ich hätte gern … — beide höflich.
Akkusativ: nur Maskulinum ändert sich (der → den, ein → einen).
Größen kommen voran: ein Stück Kuchen, ein Glas Wasser.
Zahlen: Das macht sieben Euro fünfzig.
